title: Canonical derived etale inverse-image composition is monoidal
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $u:Y\to X$ and $v:Z\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use small representatives of the small etale sites [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-etale-site], constant-coefficient module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Inverse image $u^{-1}$ is the termwise descent of the exact module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Let $\gamma_{u,v}:(uv)^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}v^{-1}u^{-1}$ be the termwise-descended inverse of the canonical module composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], normalized by the composite-adjunction unit. For each morphism $w$, write
$$\delta^w_{M,N}:w^{-1}(M\otimes^L_\Lambda N)\xrightarrow{\sim}w^{-1}M\otimes^L_\Lambda w^{-1}N$$
for the inverse of the canonical comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], where $\otimes^L_\Lambda$ is the derived tensor product of [def-kun-derived-tensor], and write $\epsilon_w:w^{-1}\underline\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline\Lambda$ for the canonical constant-sheaf comparison [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. Then, for all $M,N\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$,
$$
\delta^v_{u^{-1}M,u^{-1}N}\circ v^{-1}(\delta^u_{M,N})\circ\gamma_{u,v,M\otimes^L N}
=(\gamma_{u,v,M}\otimes^L\gamma_{u,v,N})\circ\delta^{uv}_{M,N}.
$$
The same comparison respects the unit: $\epsilon_v\circ v^{-1}(\epsilon_u)\circ\gamma_{u,v,\underline\Lambda}=\epsilon_{uv}$. For every morphism of schemes $w:V\to V'$ and $M\in D(V'_{\Et},\Lambda)$, with $l$ and $r$ the left and right unit constraints of [lem-kun-tensor-unit],
$$w^{-1}(l_M)=l_{w^{-1}M}\circ(\epsilon_w\otimes^L1)\circ\delta^w_{\underline\Lambda,M},\qquad w^{-1}(r_M)=r_{w^{-1}M}\circ(1\otimes^L\epsilon_w)\circ\delta^w_{M,\underline\Lambda}.$$
For a third morphism $t:T\to Z$, the composition comparisons satisfy
$$t^{-1}\gamma_{u,v}\circ\gamma_{uv,t}=(\gamma_{v,t}u^{-1})\circ\gamma_{u,vt}.$$
All equations use the canonical functor associativity and identity identifications and are natural in the derived objects.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, K-flat flat-term construction; underlying composition and tensor maps: sites-modules.tex Tags 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules) and 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback). The displayed coherence equations are the agent-stated comparison lemma extracted from the blueprint Kunneth-compatibility proof, not a verbatim assertion of those tags.

proof.text: Choose K-flat representatives with flat terms for the derived objects, and represent derived tensor products by their total tensor complexes. The termwise exact inverse-image functors carry these representatives and quasi-isomorphisms to the corresponding derived functors. By the K-flat tensor-descent equivalence, an equality of the natural transformations in the statement is determined by its restriction to these representatives; hence it suffices to perform the following calculations termwise on complexes of module sheaves.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 0G7D and 06YU (K-flat resolutions, flat-term localization and derived tensor); Tag 06YY (exact inverse-image factorization)

proof.text: Work termwise with sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules. For a morphism $w:V\to V'$ and module sheaves $A,B$ on $V'_{\Et}$, the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] on K-flat flat-term complexes has as constituents the isomorphisms $\kappa_w:w^{-1}A\otimes_\Lambda w^{-1}B\to w^{-1}(A\otimes_\Lambda B)$ (inverse to $\delta^w$; the module pullback is $w^{-1}$ by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (1),(2)), defined through the chain $\mathrm{Hom}(w^{-1}(A\otimes B),H)=\mathrm{Hom}(A\otimes B,w_*H)=\mathrm{Bilin}(A\times B,w_*H)=\mathrm{Bilin}(w^{-1}A\times w^{-1}B,H)=\mathrm{Hom}(w^{-1}A\otimes w^{-1}B,H)$, whose third bijection is $\Theta_w(\beta)=w_*(\beta)\circ(\eta_{w,A}\times\eta_{w,B})$ of [lem-sfb-site-inverse-image-bilinear-adjunction]. Thus, with $\tau$ the universal bilinear maps and $\varphi^\flat=w_*(\varphi)\circ\eta_w$ the adjoint of $\varphi:w^{-1}(A\otimes B)\to H$: $\Theta_w(\varphi\circ\kappa_w\circ\tau)=\varphi^\flat\circ\tau$ (*). Since $\Theta$ is injective and maps out of a tensor product are determined by their composite with $\tau$, the two maps $c_{u,v,A\otimes B}\circ v^{-1}(\kappa_u)\circ\kappa_v$ and $\kappa_{uv}\circ(c_{u,v,A}\otimes c_{u,v,B})$ from $v^{-1}u^{-1}A\otimes v^{-1}u^{-1}B$ to $(uv)^{-1}(A\otimes B)$ agree once, for every $H$ on $Z$ and every $\varphi:(uv)^{-1}(A\otimes B)\to H$, the bilinear maps obtained by composing with $\varphi$ and $\tau$ have the same image under $\Theta_u\circ\Theta_v$. Applying (*) for $v$ and then for $u$, with naturality of $\eta_v$, the first gives $u_*v_*(\varphi\circ c_{u,v})\circ u_*\eta_{v,u^{-1}}\circ\eta_u\circ\tau$. Applying $\Theta_u\Theta_v$ to $\varphi\circ\kappa_{uv}\circ\tau\circ(c\times c)$ gives $u_*v_*(\varphi\circ\kappa_{uv}\circ\tau)\circ(u_*v_*(c)u_*\eta_vu^{-1}\eta_u\times\text{same})$. By the normalization of $c_{u,v}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], $u_*v_*(c_{u,v})\circ u_*\eta_vu^{-1}\circ\eta_u=d_{u,v}\circ\eta_{uv}$; by naturality of $d_{u,v}$ (and its compatibility with products, being sectionwise) both expressions become $d_{u,v}\circ\varphi^\flat_{uv}\circ\tau$, the second by (*) for $uv$. Hence the tensor-composition square commutes on every pair of module sheaves, naturally in $A,B$. Applied to the terms $P^p,Q^q$ of K-flat flat-term complexes, it holds on every summand of the total tensor complexes (on which [def-kun-derived-tensor] computes $\otimes^L$), the Koszul signs being the same on both sides because all maps are applied summandwise.

proof.text:
Passing the termwise equality of step 2 through the K-flat tensor-descent equivalence of step 1 gives, for arbitrary M,N, exactly
$$\delta^v_{u^{-1}M,u^{-1}N}\circ v^{-1}(\delta^u_{M,N})\circ\gamma_{u,v,M\otimes^L N}=(\gamma_{u,v,M}\otimes^L\gamma_{u,v,N})\circ\delta^{uv}_{M,N}.$$ 
The equality is natural in M and N because every comparison used in the termwise calculation is natural.

source.place: Canonical tensor and composition identifications in the double-adjoint calculation; extracted tensor-composition coherence

proof.text: The constant sheaf $\underline\Lambda$ is flat and K-flat (tensoring with it is the identity up to the unit constraint), so it lies in the class of step 1 and the unit equation is the image under the localization of the degree-0 equation of module maps $\varepsilon_v\circ v^{-1}(\varepsilon_u)=\varepsilon_{uv}\circ c_{u,v,\underline\Lambda}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_Z$, where $\varepsilon_w$ is the canonical comparison of [lem-kun-pullback-constant], i.e. the map $c:w^{-1}\Lambda\to\Lambda$ of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (1), adjoint to $\gamma_w:\Lambda\to w_*\Lambda$ induced by the constant sections. Two maps out of $v^{-1}u^{-1}\Lambda_X$ are equal iff their adjoints $\Lambda_X\to u_*v_*\Lambda_Z$ under the composite adjunction (unit $u_*\eta_vu^{-1}\circ\eta_u$) are equal. By naturality of $\eta_v$, the adjoint of the left side is $u_*(\gamma_v)\circ\gamma_u$. By the normalization of $c_{u,v}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] and naturality of $d_{u,v}$, the adjoint of the right side is $d_{u,v}\circ(uv)_*(\varepsilon_{uv})\circ\eta_{uv}=d_{u,v}\circ\gamma_{uv}$. Both send the constant section $\lambda$ over $W$ to the constant section $\lambda$ of $\Lambda_Z$ over $(W\times_XY)\times_YZ$ ($d_{u,v}$ is restriction along a canonical isomorphism, which preserves constant sections), and a map out of the constant sheaf is determined by the images of constant sections (universal property of sheafification). Inverting $c$ gives $\varepsilon_v\circ v^{-1}(\varepsilon_u)\circ\gamma_{u,v,\underline\Lambda}=\varepsilon_{uv}$ in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 03D8, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules (composition of pullbacks conjugate to that of pushforwards), applied to the constant sheaf; constant sheaves via sites.tex Example 0H7J

proof.text:
Let $w:V\to V'$, $A$ a module sheaf on $V'_{\Et}$, $l_A:\Lambda\otimes A\to A$ the left unit constraint, $\lambda\otimes a\mapsto\lambda a$. Using (*) of step 2: $\Theta_w(w^{-1}(l_A)\circ\kappa_w\circ\tau)=w_*w^{-1}(l_A)\circ\eta_{w,\Lambda\otimes A}\circ\tau=\eta_{w,A}\circ l_A\circ\tau$ by naturality of $\eta_w$, i.e. $(\lambda,a)\mapsto\eta_{w,A}(\lambda a)$; and $\Theta_w(l_{w^{-1}A}\circ(\varepsilon_w\otimes1)\circ\tau)=w_*(\text{action})\circ(\gamma_w\times\eta_{w,A})$, i.e. $(\lambda,a)\mapsto\gamma_w(\lambda)\cdot\eta_{w,A}(a)$, the module structure of $w_*w^{-1}A$ being through $\gamma_w$ by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (3). The unit $\eta_{w,A}$ is $\Lambda$-linear (it is the unit of the module adjunction, same reference), so the two bilinear maps agree; by injectivity of $\Theta_w$, $w^{-1}(l_A)\circ\kappa_w=l_{w^{-1}A}\circ(\varepsilon_w\otimes1)$, i.e. $w^{-1}(l_A)=l_{w^{-1}A}\circ(\varepsilon_w\otimes1)\circ\delta^w_{\Lambda,A}$. The right unit constraint is the same computation with the factors exchanged. Applied termwise to a K-flat flat-term representative $P$ of $M$ (with $\underline\Lambda\otimes P$ the total tensor complex computing $\underline\Lambda\otimes^LM$ by [def-kun-derived-tensor], $\underline\Lambda$ being K-flat with flat terms), these are the representatives of the unit constraints of [lem-kun-tensor-unit] and of the comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]; localizing gives
$$w^{-1}(l_M)=l_{w^{-1}M}\circ(\varepsilon_w\otimes^L1)\circ\delta^w_{\underline\Lambda,M},\qquad w^{-1}(r_M)=r_{w^{-1}M}\circ(1\otimes^L\varepsilon_w)\circ\delta^w_{M,\underline\Lambda},$$
for every $M$ by step 1, naturally in $M$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, chain of bijections in its proof, evaluated on the unit; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4

proof.text:
Let $t:T\to Z$ be a third morphism. The isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (1) satisfy $u_*(d_{v,t})\circ d_{u,vt}=d_{u,v}t_*\circ d_{uv,t}:(uvt)_*\to u_*v_*t_*$: on sections over $W$ both are restriction along an isomorphism of $T$-schemes $((W\times_XY)\times_YZ)\times_ZT\to W\times_XT$ compatible with the projections to $W$ and $T$, and such an isomorphism is unique [def-pc-fibre-product]; call this map $D$. Both composites $\alpha_1=c_{uv,t}\circ t^{-1}(c_{u,v})$ and $\alpha_2=c_{u,vt}\circ c_{v,t}u^{-1}$ (isomorphisms $t^{-1}v^{-1}u^{-1}\to(uvt)^{-1}$ of module functors) satisfy $u_*v_*t_*(\alpha_i)\circ E=D\circ\eta_{uvt}$, where $E=u_*v_*\eta_tv^{-1}u^{-1}\circ u_*\eta_vu^{-1}\circ\eta_u$ is the unit of the threefold composite adjunction, which is the pasted unit by [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition]: for $\alpha_1$ apply the normalization of $c_{u,v}$, then naturality of $\eta_t$ and of $d_{u,v}$, then the normalization of $c_{uv,t}$; for $\alpha_2$ apply the normalization of $c_{v,t}$ (whiskered by $u^{-1}$ and $u_*$), then that of $c_{u,vt}$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear]. A transformation $\alpha$ with this property is unique: by adjunction $\alpha_G$ is the map whose adjoint under the threefold composite adjunction is $D\circ\eta_{uvt,G}$ (the Yoneda uniqueness of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2)). Hence $\alpha_1=\alpha_2$; inverting, $t^{-1}c_{u,v}^{-1}$ composed with $c_{uv,t}^{-1}$ equals $c_{v,t}^{-1}u^{-1}$ composed with $c_{u,vt}^{-1}$. Applying this termwise and descending by step 1 yields
$$t^{-1}\gamma_{u,v}\circ\gamma_{uv,t}=(\gamma_{v,t}u^{-1})\circ\gamma_{u,vt}.$$

All calculations use only the canonical associators and identity identifications of the total tensor complexes, so no additional symmetry or choice enters. The naturality of the module comparisons, the tensor comparison, the constant-sheaf comparison and the unit constraints passes through the localization, proving the final naturality assertion and completing all clauses of the statement.

split_report.summary: No exact project declaration states the full constant-coefficient derived pullback package. Kept the imported statement and split its proof into a K-flat representative reduction, a termwise tensor-composition calculation, the unit and left/right unit calculations, and the normalized threefold composition argument. All comparisons are extended by the existing K-flat tensor-descent equivalence; no new node was needed because the non-elementary inputs are existing DAG statements. Maintainer reader (2026-10-17): steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 rewritten to give the adjunction arguments (03EL bilinear chain via lem-sfb-site-inverse-image-bilinear-adjunction, unit normalization of c, constant sections, fibre-product coherence of d) in place of section-level assertions; statement unchanged.
blueprint: Main-20261015 Kunneth compatibility proof: the extracted tensor-composition coherence is used in the double-adjoint calculation; the present steps verify that coherence, the unit and left/right unit clauses, and associativity on K-flat representatives.

Each relied on a description at the level of sections ('on a pure tensor x(x)y both composites apply c separately'; 'the 07A4 comparison sends the unit tensor to the pulled-back unit tensor') that no cited statement gives. I rewrote both as an injectivity argument. The 03EL comparison is defined through Theta_w(beta)=w_*beta o(eta x eta) of lem-sfb-site-inverse-image-bilinear-adjunction (reviewed).
